chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) saying: 'One who acts upon what Allah has made obligatory upon him is among the best of people; and whoever avoids what Allah has forbidden him is among the most devoted of people; and whoever is content with what Allah has allotted for him is among the richest of people.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that make a person among the best, most devoted, and richest in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) defines spiritual excellence through a triad of action, restraint, and inner peace, linking outward obedience to divine law with inward contentment. This teaching, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, reflects the Shia emphasis on *Zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as a state of heart free from attachment to worldly distribution, thereby achieving true richness. It serves as a practical guide for balancing ritual duty (*Fard*) with moral vigilance (*Haram*) and psychological peace (*Qana'ah).

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 17.Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī who said, “ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (a) said, ‘

One who acts upon what Allah has made obligatory on him, he is among the best of people; and whoever eschews what Allah has forbidden him, he is among the most devoted of people; and whoever is content with what Allah has allotted for him, he is among the richest of people.’”
